source: Peggy — 'What the Top-10 Actually Accept', findings report
basis: ~5,150 self-reported applicant profiles across 10 elite universities (accepted + rejected), plus a 2,617-record verified dataset.
caveat: Self-reported and skewed STEM/high-achieving; rejected files sampled more heavily than accepted. Valid for COMPARISONS between admitted and rejected populations and between tiers — NOT as absolute admit rates.
thesis: Elite academics are the entry ticket to the pool, not the thing that wins the seat. Outcomes are decided by the tier of a student's single best achievement and by structural hooks — not by the length of the resume.

universal.claim: The academic bar is a threshold, not a differentiator. Admits and rejects both centre on 1540 SAT / 4.0 UW / 11 APs. ~36% of REJECTED applicants scored 1550+; ~16% of ADMITS scored below 1500.
universal.implication: Clear the floor, then stop. Extra points above it do not buy anything.

universal.claim: Admits list FEWER activity areas than rejects (5.8 vs 6.2). What separates them is the tier of one best achievement.
universal.implication: Depth in one thread beats a long list. Cap the activity count.

universal.claim: Structural hooks separate admits: recruited athlete 2.4x, international-level award 1.65x, ISEF/Regeneron research 1.55x, first-generation 1.5x.
universal.implication: Where a real hook exists, build around it. Never assert a hook the student does not actually hold.
universal.caution: The report does not state whether 'first-generation' means first-gen COLLEGE or first-gen immigrant. Do not apply it to a student with college-graduate parents until that is resolved.

universal.claim: Students who struck out across all top-10s over-index on volunteer HOURS, AP-Scholar, and the international pool.
universal.implication: Logged service hours are not a lever. Sustained involvement in one cause is.

universal.claim: Signals rise monotonically Top 21-50 -> 11-20 -> Top 10; a top-10 profile cascades downward and collects the lower tiers automatically.
universal.implication: Build for the top of the realistic range; the rest follows.

humanities.note: National / international awards plus an arts & writing portfolio (not olympiads).

social_science.note: Most score-sensitive of the non-STEM tracks; RESEARCH + DEBATE (42% of top-10 admits).

business.note: LOWEST academic bar of any track; LEADERSHIP / DEBATE outweigh research.
